anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level statement or transaction design forces the engine to scan or manipulate more data than necessary, inflating execution time and resource footprint.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: Engine and session memory segments expand beyond safe host limits, provoking paging, cache churn, or OOM-related terminations.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: Client–server communication paths or connection slots become saturated or unstable, causing slow or failed connection establishment and data transfer.

When all three anomalies arise concurrently, the database exhibits extreme and erratic latency: long-running, chatty, or over-fetching SQL drives large in-memory work areas and swollen buffer/plan caches, which in turn intensify OS memory pressure and trigger swapping or OOM kills. At the same time, bloated result sets and prolonged transaction lifetimes monopolize network sockets and listener threads, increasing connection queue depths, client-side timeouts, retransmissions, and a surge in aborted or half-open sessions. Monitoring views show simultaneous spikes in memory consumption, cache churn, statement and transaction wait times, and network wait events, making it difficult to attribute delays to any single layer.

Causally, inefficient workload logic amplifies memory demand (e.g., wide scans, large sorts, oversized batches), accelerating the onset of memory exhaustion. Memory pressure then slows processing and may force result spilling, lengthening data-transfer windows and holding connections open longer. Prolonged or stalled transfers consume additional network buffers and connection slots, which feed back into the application layer as retries that spawn even more SQL statements and sessions. These cascaded effects create a feedback loop where bad SQL inflates memory use, memory contention throttles throughput, and constrained connectivity magnifies latency and retry storms, jointly degrading overall database stability and performance.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle, but not within an open transaction, for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle and not inside an open transaction longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; the documentation warns about using this with connection pools or middleware.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
